Thanks — below is a 12-week progressive hypertrophy program designed for a 26-year-old female recreational lifter who is strictly vegan and wants to gain muscle while hitting 150 g protein/day from plant-only sources. Program assumes access to a full gym. I include phases, weekly structure, per-session exercise lists with sets/reps/tempo and progression guidance, plus a practical vegan meal and supplementation plan to reach 150 g protein/d and recovery guidance.

Important notes before starting
- If she has any injuries, medical conditions, or is pregnant, adjust or clear with a health professional first.
- Track bodyweight, training loads (weights used), and measurements every 2 weeks. Aim to add load or reps each week on main lifts when possible.
- Warm-up before each session: 5–10 minutes light cardio + dynamic mobility focusing on target joints, plus 1–2 warm-up sets for each main compound lift.
- Rest between sets: 60–90s for accessory work, 90–120s for heavier compound sets.
- Tempo: where not specified, use controlled 2‑0‑1 (eccentric 2s, no pause, concentric 1s). For some exercises I specify different tempos.
- Ensure progressive overload via more weight, more reps, better form, or slightly reduced rest.

Program overview
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week, upper/lower split (balanced for hypertrophy).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4: Foundation (volume build, technique, work capacity)
  - Weeks 5–8: Hypertrophy focus (higher intensity and targeted volume)
  - Weeks 9–12: Intensification + accumulation (slightly higher load, some density work and microcycles to push growth)
- Each week: 2× upper, 2× lower. Optional short conditioning session once weekly (10–20 min HIIT or low-impact cardio) if recovery allows.
- Deload: Week 8 has an optional reduced volume day if fatigue accumulates (I’ll note recovery checks).

Weekly calendar (example)
- Monday: Upper A
- Tuesday: Lower A
- Wednesday: Rest or active recovery (walking, mobility)
- Thursday: Upper B
- Friday: Lower B
- Sat: Optional conditioning / mobility or rest
- Sun: Rest

Detailed week-by-week program

Weeks 1–4: Foundation (build work capacity, technique, baseline volume)
Goal: 8–12 reps for main hypertrophy, establish form and consistent progressive overload.

Upper A (Mon)
1. Barbell bench press — 4 sets x 6–10 reps (build to a challenging set in that range). Tempo 2-0-1.
2. Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 8–12
3. Seated cable row (or barbell row) — 4 x 8–12
4. Lat pulldown (wide) — 3 x 8–12
5. Dumbbell lateral raise — 3 x 12–15
6. Face pulls — 3 x 12–15
7. Triceps rope pushdown or dips — 3 x 10–12
8. Hammer curls — 3 x 10–12

Lower A (Tue)
1. Barbell back squat — 4 x 6–10
2. Romanian deadlift — 3 x 8–10
3. Bulgarian split squat — 3 x 8–10 per leg
4. Leg press — 3 x 10–12
5. Seated or standing calf raise — 4 x 12–15
6. Ab wheel or hanging leg raises — 3 x 10–15

Upper B (Thu)
1. Overhead press (barbell or dumbbell) — 4 x 6–10
2. Flat dumbbell press or close-grip bench — 3 x 8–12
3. One-arm dumbbell row — 4 x 8–12 per arm
4. Pull-ups or assisted pull-ups — 3 x 6–10 (or lat pulldown if needed)
5. Rear delt fly (cable or machine) — 3 x 12–15
6. EZ-bar curls or preacher curls — 3 x 8–12
7. Skullcrushers or overhead triceps extension — 3 x 8–12

Lower B (Fri)
1. Deadlift (conventional or trap bar) — 3–4 x 4–8 (start conservative; focus on form)
2. Front squat or goblet squat — 3 x 6–10
3. Hamstring curl (lying or seated) — 3 x 10–12
4. Walking lunges — 3 x 10–12 per leg
5. Glute bridge or hip thrust — 3 x 8–12
6. Standing calf raise — 4 x 12–15
7. Plank 3 x 45–60s

Progression Wks 1–4
- Add 1–2.5 kg (2–5 lb) to compound lifts if you hit upper end of rep range with good form for two sessions in a row.
- If not, add 1–2 reps the next session until you can increase weight.
- Emphasize full range of motion and tempo.

Nutrition targets and plan to hit 150 g protein/day (vegan)
- Calories: To gain muscle, start with a modest surplus: approx. maintenance + 250–400 kcal/day. If unknown, estimate maintenance ~ bodyweight (kg) × 33 kcal for active recreational lifter, then add 300 kcal.
- Protein: 150 g/day (approx. 2.0–2.2 g/kg if she’s ~70 kg — adjust to weight). Prioritize even distribution: aim for ~30–40 g protein per meal, with 3–5 meals/snacks.
- Carbs and fat: Fill remaining calories with carbs for training performance and healthy fats (omega-3 from algae oil). Aim ~45–55% calories from carbs, 25–35% from fat.

Practical vegan protein sources (and approximate protein per serving)
- Soy/tofu: firm tofu 1 cup cooked ~20 g
- Tempeh: 100 g ~19–20 g
- Seitan: 100 g ~25 g
- Textured vegetable protein (TVP): 1 cup cooked ~12 g (varies)
- Legumes: lentils 1 cup cooked ~18 g; chickpeas 1 cup cooked ~15 g; black beans 1 cup ~15 g
- Vegan protein powders: pea, rice, soy blends ~20–25 g per scoop (read label)
- Plant-based yogurt: 150–200 g often ~6–10 g (varies by brand, some fortified soy yogurts higher)
- Nuts/seeds: 2 tbsp almond butter ~7 g; hemp seeds 3 tbsp ~10 g; chia seeds 2 tbsp ~5 g
- Whole grains: quinoa 1 cup cooked ~8 g; oats 1 cup cooked ~6 g
- Nutritional yeast: 2 tbsp ~8 g (flakey/tasty on savory dishes)

Sample daily meal template to reach 150 g protein
- Breakfast (35–45 g):
  - Tofu scramble (200 g firm tofu ≈ 26 g) with nutritional yeast (2 tbsp ≈ 8 g) + 1 cup oats with almond milk and 1 scoop vegan protein (20–25 g) — pick combos to reach target. Example: 1 scoop protein (22 g) + 150 g tofu (20 g) + 1 tbsp nutritional yeast (4 g) spread across morning = ~46 g. Adjust portions.
- Snack (15–25 g):
  - Smoothie: 1 scoop vegan protein (22 g) + 1 tbsp peanut butter (4–8 g) + fruit + oats.
- Lunch (30–40 g):
  - Tempeh bowl: 150 g tempeh (~30 g) + quinoa (1 cup cooked ≈ 8 g) + veg + tahini dressing.
- Snack (10–15 g):
  - Hummus (1/2 cup ~10 g) + whole-grain pita or edamame (1 cup shelled edamame ~17 g).
- Dinner (25–35 g):
  - Stir-fry with seitan (100–150 g seitan ~25–37 g) or lentil/dal + rice + veg.
- Optional before-bed snack (10–15 g):
  - Casein isn’t available; use pea-protein shake with soy milk or peanut butter and oats, or high-protein soy yogurt.

Example concrete menu (approximate protein)
- Breakfast: Smoothie — 1 scoop pea/rice protein (22 g), 250 ml soy milk (8 g), 2 tbsp hemp seeds (10 g) = 40 g
- Snack: 150 g edamame = 17 g
- Lunch: 200 g tempeh bowl (40 g) with quinoa = 48 g (tempeh 200 g ≈ 40 g, quinoa 1/2 cup ≈ 4 g)
- Snack: Hummus + veggies + handful almonds = ~8–10 g
- Dinner: Lentil dal with seitan or large portion lentils (1.5 cups cooked lentils ≈ 27 g) + tofu side = 40 g
Total ≈ 145–155 g depending on portions — adjust exact portions to reach 150 g.

Supplements (vegan-friendly)
- Vegan protein powder (pea/soy/rice blend) to help hit protein goals.
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day (vegan-safe) — supports strength & hypertrophy.
- Vitamin B12 supplement (essential for strict vegans).
- Vitamin D if low (D3 algae-based if possible).
- Omega-3 (algal DHA/EPA) 250–500 mg recommended.
- Consider iron status monitoring; supplement if low (with professional guidance). Also check calcium intake.

Weeks 5–8: Hypertrophy (increase intensity and targeted volume)
Goal: Slightly higher per-muscle volume, increase time under tension and include drop sets/longer sets on week 7–8.

Training changes: Move main compounds to 3–5 sets in 6–10 rep ranges with one heavier set (5–8 reps) per main lift. Increase accessory volume to 10–20 sets per muscle group per week (upper/lower balanced).

Upper A (Mon)
1. Barbell bench press — 5 x 5–8 (work up to heavy set)
2. Incline dumbbell press — 3 x 8–12
3. Chest-supported row — 4 x 8–12
4. Weighted pull-up or lat pulldown — 4 x 6–10
5. Lateral raises — 4 x 12–15 (last set drop set optional)
6. Face pulls — 4 x 12–15
7. Triceps superset: close-grip pushups 3 x 10 + rope pushdowns 3 x 12

Lower A (Tue)
1. Back squat — 5 x 5–8
2. Romanian deadlift — 4 x 6–10
3. Bulgarian split squat — 4 x 8–10
4. Leg curl — 3 x 10–12
5. Hip thrust — 3 x 8–10
6. Calf raises — 5 x 10–15
7. Core: weighted plank 3 x 45s

Upper B (Thu)
1. Overhead press — 5 x 5–8
2. Close-grip bench or incline DB press — 3 x 8–12
3. Single-arm row — 4 x 8–12
4. Cable pulldown (neutral grip) — 3 x 8–12
5. Rear delt + lateral superset — 3 x 12–15 each
6. Biceps focus: barbell curl 4 x 8–12
7. Triceps: overhead rope extension 3 x 10–12

Lower B (Fri)
1. Deadlift — 4 x 4–6 (heavier relative intensity)
2. Front squat or goblet — 3 x 6–8
3. Walking lunges — 4 x 10 per leg
4. Glute-ham raise or Nordic curl — 3 x 6–10
5. Hip thrust — 3 x 8–10 (drop set last set optional)
6. Calves & core as before

Progression Wks 5–8
- Continue to add weight or reps. Week 8 can be a reduced-volume deload week if fatigue is high: cut volume 30–40% and keep intensity moderate.

Nutrition notes (during weeks 5–8)
- If muscle/weight gains are slower than desired after 3–4 weeks, increase calories by 150–250 kcal/day.
- Continue protein at 150 g/day, maintain even distribution.
- Ensure post-workout meal or shake includes 20–40 g protein and carbs (e.g., protein shake + banana, or tempeh + rice).

Weeks 9–12: Intensification + accumulation (final 4-week push)
Goal: Build maximum attainable muscle; add some higher intensity/volume mixing; finish with a final week to re-test 1–3 rep max on main lifts if desired for progress tracking (optional).

Training changes: Use wave-style loading: week 9 slightly higher reps (8–12), week 10 heavier (5–8), week 11 mixed, week 12 taper (reduce volume 10–20% but keep intensity to allow strength display).

Weeks 9–12 example progression
Week 9 (higher volume)
Upper A
1. Bench press — 4 x 8–10
2. Incline DB — 4 x 8–10
3. Bent-over row — 4 x 8–10
4. Pull-ups/pulldowns — 3 x 8–10
5. Lateral raises — 4 x 12–15
6. Face pulls — 4 x 12–15
7. Arms superset — 3 x 10–12 each

Lower A
1. Squat — 4 x 8–10
2. RDL — 4 x 8–10
3. Bulgarian split — 4 x 10
4. Leg press — 3 x 12–15
5. Hip thrust — 4 x 8–12
6. Calves/core: higher rep sets

Week 10 (heavier)
Upper A
1. Bench press — 5 x 5–7
... (mirror earlier but heavier; focus on progressive overload)

Week 11 (mixed)
- Use heavier compound sets plus higher-rep finishing sets and techniques such as rest-pause (e.g., after final set reduce weight ~20% and do 6–8 more reps), or short drop sets for accessory muscles.

Week 12 (taper/test or consolidation)
- Reduce overall volume 10–20%, keep some heavy sets for strength validation. Do a 1–3RM test only if client feels recovered and technique is solid. Otherwise, keep sessions lighter and focus on high-quality hypertrophy work.

Recovery and accessory guidance
- Sleep: aim 7–9 hours/night.
- Hydration: at least 2–3 L/day, more around workouts.
- Foam rolling and mobility: 2–3 sessions/week, 10–15 min.
- Active recovery: light walks, yoga, or swimming on rest days if desired.
- Massage/soft-tissue work monthly or as needed.

Trackable metrics and progression plan
- Train logs: record exercises, sets, reps, RPE, and weight. Aim to improve one of those metrics per session.
- Bodyweight and circumference measurements every 2 weeks.
- Adjust calorie intake +50–150 kcal if gains stalled for 2 weeks or excessive fat gain occurs.

Example grocery list (protein-focused)
- Tofu, tempeh, seitan
- Canned/fresh lentils, chickpeas, black beans
- Frozen edamame
- Vegan protein powder (pea/soy blend)
- Oats, quinoa, brown rice
- Nutritional yeast, tahini
- Nuts & nut butters, hemp/chia/flax seeds
- Soy milk or other high-protein plant milks
- Veggies and fruit
- Algae omega-3, B12, creatine monohydrate

Final notes and tailoring
- I can convert this into a printable week-by-week sheet with specific weights, rest times, and progress templates if you tell me the client’s current training maxes (e.g., 1RM or working sets) and bodyweight.
- If she prefers 5 days/week or wants more conditioning, I can adapt volume and layout.
- If hitting 150 g protein is a challenge, I can give 7–10 specific meal recipes with exact macros to ensure compliance.

Would you like:
- A 12-week printable PDF with daily sessions and spaces to log loads/reps?
- Specific meal recipes and shopping list with exact portion sizes to reach 150 g protein/day calibrated to her bodyweight?
